evidence_scope: Visible scalar Dopesheet tracks and measured mouse/keyboard gestures for initialized local arrays and captured aliases with local projections. The broader Composer goal remains active.
tested_behavior: Show combined, X and Y as distinct tracks. Markers retain logical channel names and exact clocks, with no copies of authored values in the display cache.
Use component identity for actual box/Shift selection, move ghosts, scale ghosts, Alt copy, Ctrl+D copy, between-key selection, focused tracks and keyboard Delete.
Move mixed selected X/Y keys and update canonical owners and captured alias projections together. Preserve combined keys and unselected keys.
Replace a Y collision at the same clock as X while preserving the complete X channel. Publish selection with the correct axis and clock.
Ctrl+Alt scaling and Ctrl+D multi-axis copying retain component channels. Copies clear source IDs and drivers while originals retain them.
Ctrl+A captures every displayed combined/scalar channel. One Delete transaction deduplicates canonical physical keys selected through owner and alias identities.
Undo/redo recover exact documents. Stale full pins and refused history admission preserve authored data and selection, and allow a later retry.
A combined clipboard focused onto a scalar row refuses before gesture staging, preserving clipboard, document and history until component-target paste is supported.
Rebuild the display cache atomically under total-key, byte and weighted name-work admission. Invalid scalar clocks refuse without replacing the retained cache.
The existing Composer workflow now locates its trigger by full marker identity instead of a removed combined-array index.
Double-click between two keys selects both endpoints on the same alias Y channel; Ctrl+C captures both correct component pins without changing history.
